post.description: Exchanges an email address and password for an access token and a new session. The Web client accepts only administrators and receives the refresh token in the fs_refresh cookie; the Mobile client accepts only technicians and receives it in the body.
Rotates the refresh token and issues a new access token. The Web client sends no body, the fs_refresh cookie and the X-FieldService-Csrf header; the Mobile client sends its refresh token in the body.

Revokes the session that the refresh credential belongs to. The Web client sends the fs_refresh cookie and the X-FieldService-Csrf header, and the response clears the cookie; the Mobile client sends its refresh token in the body. A missing, unknown, expired or revoked credential also returns 204.

Issues a ticket for one connection attempt to the notification service's Socket.IO endpoint. The ticket is valid for 60 seconds and is accepted once; every call issues a new ticket. Send no body. The access token's session must still be live and its user active; a revoked or expired session, or an inactive user, returns 401 auth.session-expired.

get.description: Returns every technician, ordered by name, with trade, shift, whether they can be assigned now, their count of open jobs, their current job in progress or on hold, and their next assigned job.

Returns the jobs assigned to the calling technician, and never another technician's. The active view, the default, holds Assigned, InProgress and OnHold jobs ordered by scheduled start, then job number. The completed view holds Completed and Cancelled jobs ordered by last update with the newest first, at most 50.

post.description: Creates a job with the next job number and a Created history entry. Without a technician the job starts Unassigned. With a technician, who must be active and on shift, it starts Assigned and also gets an Assigned history entry at the same instant. The response carries the job's details and version, and its Location header points to the job.

get.description: Returns one page of jobs that match every filter, ordered by last update with the newest first, with the total count and the count for each status under every filter except status. The search matches the job number, title, customer and site address.
Returns the job with its assignee, its complete history, oldest first, and the version to send with the next command. A technician can read only the jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404.

put.summary: Assign a job to a technician
put.description: Assigns an unassigned job, or reassigns an assigned job, to an active technician who is on shift, and adds an Assigned history entry. Send the version you last read; assigning the same technician again returns the job unchanged. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

put.summary: Update the status of a job
put.description: Starts, puts on hold or resumes a job assigned to the calling technician, and adds a Started, PutOnHold or Resumed history entry. The status must be InProgress or OnHold. Putting a job on hold needs a note of at most 500 characters; a note sent with InProgress is not stored. Send the version you last read; sending the job's current status returns the job unchanged. A technician can change only the jobs assigned to them; any other job returns 404. The response carries the job's details and its new version.

get.description: Returns every checklist template, ordered by name, with its trade and item count. The create-job form offers them as the job's checklist.
